item.title: Sweden to increase deportations of convicted immigrants
item.description: Sweden's government on Wednesday said it wanted to drastically increase the number of immigrants deported after being convicted, saying any crime with a penalty higher than a fine should lead to a deportation as a rule.

item.title: Tenant in Sweden gets 144,000 kronor back from rent over-payment
item.description: A tenant in central Gothenburg is getting a lot of money back after a rental board ruled in her favour.

item.title: NEW: The Local’s self-paced Swedish course
item.description: Due to popular demand The Local's self-paced online Swedish course for beginners is back, designed to make learning flexible and practical.

item.title: 'Serious threat' to Nordic energy infrastructure reported in Sweden
item.description: A serious threat was on Thursday directed at energy infrastructure in all Nordic countries, according to Swedish media reports. Sweden's national defence agency has since said that there is no specific present threat to the country's energy infrastructure.

item.title: How to influence political decisions on Sweden's new citizenship rules
item.description: A number of The Local's readers have reached out since more details of the planned changes to Swedish citizenship rules were unveiled in February asking how they can share their opinions with decision-makers. Here are a few ways to do so.

item.title: Sweden's Migration Minister says 'no' to proposal to stop teen deportations
item.description: Migration Minister Johan Forssell has given a flat "no" to a stop law put forward by the opposition on the much-debated teenage deportations. The opposition's attempt to get such a law passed will be decided next week.

item.title: Swedish word of the day: nyanlända
item.description: Although today's word of the day technically means 'new arrivals', in practice it's used slightly differently.

item.title: How to get your money back if you've been paying too much rent in Sweden
item.description: The cost of sublets in Sweden has soared over the past decade, so what should you do if you think you've been overcharged?

item.title: OPINION: 'Sweden's parliament should add transitional rules to the citizenship law'
item.description: If Sweden’s parliament passes a new citizenship law without transitional rules, it risks undermining the reputation for fairness and stability that has long helped Sweden attract skilled international workers, says Patrick Gallen, spokesperson of the Fair Transition campaign.

item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Friday
item.description: Swedish PM says government to set up inquiry on teen deportations, Sweden open to hosting nuclear weapons in wartime, and other news from Sweden on Friday.
